title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: Every dead code check in one sweep
summary: Kotlin Jump 1.38.0 gathers every dead code check into one workspace scan, and can clear what it finds in a single previewable change.

highlights.title: One Scan, Every Check
highlights.description: A new "Find Dead Code" command sweeps the workspace for unused imports, parameters, private declarations, local variables, and write-only variables at once, and tells you how many of each it found.

highlights.title: Where Dead Code Hides
highlights.description: Findings are reported for the files you do not have open, which is where dead code accumulates. A file you open keeps its own live warnings rather than showing everything twice.

highlights.title: Clear It in One Preview
highlights.description: "Clean Dead Code in This File" and "Clean Dead Code in the Workspace" remove everything with a safe fix in one step, always through the Refactor Preview so nothing is applied unseen.

sections.heading: Improvements
bullets: Adds the "Kotlin Jump: Find Dead Code" command, which sweeps the whole workspace for unused imports, parameters, private declarations, local variables, and write-only variables at once, and reports the total per category.
Reports findings for files you do not have open, where dead code actually accumulates; a file you open keeps its own live warnings instead of showing everything twice.

Adds "Kotlin Jump: Clean Dead Code in This File" and "Clean Dead Code in the Workspace", removing everything that has a safe fix in one step, always through the Refactor Preview so nothing is applied unseen.
Skips a finding whenever two checks disagree about the same range, so a sweep can never make an edit that no single check would have made on its own.

sections.heading: Fixes
bullets: Fixes write-only variable detection inside a method whose name matches a scope function, such as fun run() or fun apply(). Those methods were treated as run { } and apply { } blocks, which silenced the check across every Runnable implementation.
